title: Tech Note: Creating Mashups with 4D Live Window
author: Joseph Resuello, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Web_SetURL / Web_GetURL / Web_Back / Web_Forward / Web_GetContent / Web_SetPreferences

historical_commentary.text: This note captures the Web 2.0-era enthusiasm for 'mashups' by embedding a native browser control (4D Live Window) into a 4D form and driving its URL from record data, essentially an early form of API/webview integration years before responsive web components or ORDA existed. The specific plug-in, the 4D Web 2.0 Pack, and the third-party URL formats referenced (old Google Maps and FedEx URL schemes) are long obsolete, but the underlying pattern of embedding a browser control in a desktop form to surface live external data remains conceptually relevant and is still done today with modern web area/webview components in 4D.
related_updates: The 4D Web 2.0 Pack and its 4D Live Window plug-in were discontinued and superseded by 4D's built-in Web Area / Web Server form objects
Google Maps, FedEx, and UPCDatabase.com have all since replaced the URL-based query formats referenced in the note with modern REST/JavaScript APIs
Embedding external web content in 4D forms is now typically done with 4D's native Web Area object rather than a third-party plug-in
